title: fix: hide failing community models without disabling them
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Renames the community endpoint state and audit fields from disabled to hidden while preserving existing data
- Keeps hidden models callable by exact ID but removes them from catalogs and community fallback targets
- Updates the owner dashboard and Account API to use hide and relist semantics
- Updates the EC2 monitor policy, SQL, cadence, and prompts to hide unhealthy models without auto-relisting
- Codifies the 300k Claude context window and repo-managed monitor updates

Checks:
- Full Gen test suite and typecheck
- Enter changed-file typecheck and billing registry tests
- Monitor JavaScript and shell syntax
- Biome and CodeQL

gist.headline: The catalog stopped recommending wilted flowers
gist.blurb: Community models that need a quiet recovery now step out of the public catalog without being uprooted. Their exact IDs still work; the fallback garden simply stops sending visitors toward the droopy leaves.
gist.summary: Renamed community-model disabling to hiding, so unhealthy models are removed from catalogs and fallback targets while remaining callable by exact ID, with owner-dashboard, Account API, database, and monitor support for hide/relist semantics.
gist.impact: Users get cleaner model catalogs and more reliable community fallbacks, while model owners can relist recovered endpoints without losing their existing model IDs or data.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy community-model garden where Polli acts as a thoughtful gardener, gently drawing a curtain around a wilted code-flower rather than removing it. A retro catalog terminal and cheerful healthy code-plants show that the public path and fallback garden stay tidy, while a small exact-ID key tag remains attached to the hidden plant to show it is still reachable directly.
